Stablecoins and Cross-Border Payments: How Digital Dollars Move Across Borders
We'd love your feedback.
Stablecoins are a type of cryptocurrency designed to hold a fixed value against a reference currency, most commonly one U.S. dollar.
Transferring stablecoins across countries is unlike transferring money through a bank: A sender converts their local currency into a stablecoin, sends it to the recipient’s blockchain address via a blockchain network, and the recipient then converts it to their own local currency. Recently, this is being recognized as an often more efficient and cost-effective method of moving money for international remittances.
In this article, we’ll cover the mechanics, benefits, and drawbacks of stablecoins in cross-border payments.
What Is a Stablecoin, and Why Does It Matter for Payments?
A stablecoin is a token that promises redemption at par against a reference currency, backed by reserves the issuer holds in cash and short-term government debt. Almost the entirety of the stablecoin market is based on US Dollars, with Tether's USDT and Circle's USDC forming a duopoly that accounts for over 85% of the market.
Stablecoins are useful for payments because they are pegged to a single stable value and can be transacted anytime, anywhere, without an intermediary like a bank. This gives them certain advantages over traditional payment rails.
Why Are Traditional Cross-Border Payments Slow and Expensive?
Traditional cross-border payments, or bank remittances, are slow and expensive because they require multiple compliance checks, processing times, and fees across multiple parties. They are also limited by the bank’s working hours. For example, a payment done on a Friday afternoon in New York cannot reach its recipient in Mumbai until the next business day on Monday.
How Do Stablecoin Cross-Border Payments Work?
A stablecoin payment has three legs:
- The On-Ramp: A business or consumer deposits local currency to a licensed stablecoin provider, oftentimes crypto exchanges, brokers, or payment platforms, who convert the currency into stablecoins.
- The Onchain Transfer: The stablecoins move from the sender's wallet to the recipient's wallet via the blockchain, which often takes seconds to a few minutes depending on the network.
- The Off-Ramp: The recipient can then convert the stablecoins, via similar crypto exchanges, brokers, or payment platforms, into their respective local currency. It is worth noting that this part of the transaction is where most of the friction and added costs are, because local platform liquidity can be dry and foreign FX spreads can be costly.
Compliance and Screening
The firms that operate the stablecoin on- and off-ramps are responsible for compliance obligations, as they are tasked with monitoring wallet addresses against sanctions lists and filing the same reports a traditional money transmitter would.
Which Cross-Border Use Cases Have Actually Worked?
Business-to-business (B2B) payments are the largest example, with treasury management being the second, where companies can move liquidity between their own international entities and wallets without having to wait for traditional banking hours.
Payouts from freelance marketplaces are also a notable example, as freelancers based in countries with weak, highly inflationary currencies can choose to be paid in the relatively stronger US Dollar via stablecoins.
Consumer remittances are the most famous example, but actually account for the least volume. BVNK, which processed about $30 billion in annualized stablecoin payment volume in 2025, reports that most of its flow is B2B rather than person-to-person, likely because P2P stablecoin transfer sizes on consumer apps are worth $47 on average, compared to ~$250 for a traditional remittance.
Who Is Building Stablecoin Payment Rails?
Issuers and Their Networks
Circle launched the Circle Payments Network (CPN) in 2025 to connect banks, payment service providers, and virtual asset firms into one settlement layer.
Remittance Companies
Western Union launched a stablecoin in May 2026, issued by Anchorage Digital Bank on Solana. Bitso also reported processing over $6.5 billion of US-to-Mexico remittances in 2024
Card Networks and Processors
Visa accepts stablecoins and allows some cardholders to spend USDC at merchants. Mastercard also added intraday, weekend, and holiday card settlement in six regulated stablecoins across eight blockchains in the United States and Latin America. Stripe bought the stablecoin infrastructure firm Bridge for $1.1 billion, extended stablecoin acceptance to merchants in more than 100 countries, and backed Tempo, a blockchain built specifically for payments.
Emerging Market Fintechs
Providers in the corridors themselves have built much of the working infrastructure. Nigeria's Paga is deploying stablecoin payments for freelancers and businesses paying overseas suppliers; Nigeria accounts for roughly 60% of stablecoin inflows into sub-Saharan Africa since 2019, according to the IMF.
How Much Cross-Border Volume Actually Moves on Stablecoins?
Of roughly $35 trillion in annualized stablecoin transaction volume, it is estimated that just less than 1% represented genuine payments such as supplier invoices, remittances, payroll, and card spending.
The remaining 99% represented trading and on-chain activity such as arbitrage, bridging and bots. These are still the primary use cases of stablecoins, while cross-border payments and other real-world utility remains in a proof-of-concept phase.
What Are the Risks and Limits of Cross-Border Stablecoin Payments?
- Off-Ramp Liquidity and Local FX: While the blockchain leg is fast and cheap, converting tokens into emerging market currencies in large amounts may not be possible due to high FX spreads and low liquidity.
- Reserve and Redemption Risk: A stablecoin holds its peg as long as the market believes the issuer has sufficient reserves and can redeem on demand. For example, USDC broke its peg in March 2023 when Silicon Valley Bank failed, before recovering days later.
- Accounting and Tax Treatment: A single company paying suppliers across Brazil, India, and Nigeria may face three different accounting treatments for the same stablecoin transaction. Finance teams have to reconcile token movements against fiat books, and guidance in many emerging markets is still incomplete.
- Issuer Concentration: Tether and Circle together account for nearly 90% of total stablecoin supply, and a payment network built on just two issuers naturally inherits their operational and regulatory risks.
How Are Stablecoin Cross-Border Payments Regulated?
Regulation now runs through licensing regimes for issuers, and the frameworks differ enough to shape which tokens can be used in which jurisdiction. In the United States, stablecoins are governed by the GENIUS Act, while Europe has MiCA.
How Are Banks Responding?
Banks are building tokenized deposits rather than adopting stablecoins. A tokenized deposit is commercial bank money recorded on a blockchain, held on the issuing bank's balance sheet and covered by deposit insurance. On the other hand, a stablecoin is a claim on a non-bank issuer's reserve pool.
U.S. banks such as JPMorgan, Citigroup, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, and more than a dozen others announced a tokenized deposit network through The Clearing House in June 2026, targeting a launch in the first half of 2027.
Although not an example of stablecoin adoption, these examples do show that banks are responding to the benefits that blockchain rails offer over traditional banking.
What Should Institutions Evaluate Before Using Stablecoin Rails?
Case-by-case cost comparisons. For example, a stablecoin payment rail that looks 4% cheaper on the blockchain leg can turn out to be more expensive after local currency conversion spreads, with pricing varying sharply by country and payout method.

Will AI solve the productivity puzzle? With Nick Bloom
Roula Khalaf, Editor of the FT, selects her favourite stories in this weekly newsletter.
Productivity has been a problem for the past 15 years. In developed countries, weak demand, a lack of competition and a paucity of new ideas have all been blamed. Could AI finally reverse that trend? Soumaya speaks to Stanford economics professor Nick Bloom about why CFOs and CEOs expect AI to supercharge their businesses; how concentrated (or otherwise) the gains might be; and why working from home could be good for labour output… and fertility rates.

title: Anthropic says its own AI models breached three companies during security tests
summary: After OpenAI's models broke into Hugging Face, Anthropic checked its own history and found three similar incidents
full_text:
Anthropic said Thursday that an internal investigation uncovered three incidents in which its AI model Claude breached the systems of three organizations while conducting cybersecurity tests. The investigation, and disclosure, comes more than a week after OpenAI disclosed that one of its unreleased models breached Hugging Face’s systems during internal testing.
In all three cases, a Claude model reached the internet from within a testing environment while interacting with a third party and then gained unauthorized access to the live systems of these organizations, Anthropic said in a blog post, describing what it found and what the company plans to change to prevent this from happening again.
Anthropic said the July 21 OpenAI incident prompted the company to conduct its own cybersecurity evaluation. It specifically looked for evidence that Claude had accessed the internet from within testing environments, which are designed to act as sandboxes and keep models isolated.
Among the 141,006 evaluation runs it reviewed, the AI lab found three incidents in which its model accessed the internet while interacting with Irregular, one of its third-party partners. Anthropic said the access traced back to a misconfiguration in the evaluation environment run with Irregular. It called this a “misunderstanding” between the two companies over whether the test setup had internet access, when in fact it did. Anthropic said it isn’t placing blame and is “approaching the fixes as if the responsibility were ours alone,” while observing that Irregular is conducting its own separate investigation.
Either way, because of that open connection, the model gained unauthorized access to the production infrastructure of three different organizations. Anthropic said the incidents involved three different Claude models: Opus 4.7, Mythos 5, and an internal research test model.
Notably, Anthropic said that in each of these cases “Claude was explicitly told by our prompt that it had no internet access.” It appears that the AI model assumed real-world systems to be part of the exercise it was asked to perform.
That assumption didn’t hold up uniformly, as it turns out. The three models didn’t behave the same way once evidence emerged that their targets were real, which Anthropic flagged as one of the more eye-opening findings.
Opus 4.7, the oldest of the three, recognized that it had reached a real production system in all four runs of that incident. In two of them, it rationalized that the real company must somehow be part of the exercise, but in all four, it kept attacking anyway, including pulling credentials and touching a database of production data. Mythos 5 also picked up on signs that it was on the real internet, but it talked itself back into believing it was still in a simulation, going on to publish a malicious software package to the public Python software registry PyPI, which was downloaded and run by outside systems before being caught. Only the internal research test model, Anthropic’s newest, stopped on its own once it concluded the target was real.
In response, Anthropic said significant controls must be placed on these kinds of evaluations if powerful AI models are involved, echoing some sentiments within the cybersecurity community.
The company also noted that Claude was running without the additional safety monitoring and classifiers it deploys on generally available models, safeguards it said would have blocked the behavior, because the evaluations are designed to measure the underlying model’s raw capabilities.
Importantly, Anthropic said it found no evidence of any model “pursuing a goal of its own” and instead merely tried to complete the task it was asked to do.
Though comparisons between the two incidents are inevitable, Anthropic drew a clear distinction between its incidents and OpenAI’s, noting where OpenAI’s model exploited an unknown software vulnerability to break out of its test environment, Anthropic’s models instead reached the internet through a path that had, by mistake, been left open.
OpenAI has continued to release new details about its own breach, saying its models also used publicly exposed credentials across four accounts on four services: one as a staging point, one for storage, and two that were only looked at, not used to break in further, according to OpenAI’s own updated blog post about the incident.
Anthropic also drew a distinction between itself and OpenAI by noting that it discovered the incidents itself, through a proactive review, and that the two affected organizations it was able to reach hadn’t previously detected the activity or flagged it to Anthropic.
The company added that it’s now working with the independent evaluation group METR on a third-party review of the incidents.
OpenAI’s accidental breach of Hugging Face, which was the first verifiable case of an AI lab losing control of its model, sparked a string of reactions from the industry and politicians, many of whom don’t necessarily agree with one another. This latest disclosure from Anthropic ensures the debate over AI models and security will continue.

title: Anthropic Says Claude Hacked 3 Organizations During Cybersecurity Tests
summary: In a review triggered by OpenAI’s Hugging Face incident, Anthropic discovered three of its AI models had breached real organizations during third-party evaluations.
full_text:
Anthropic disclosed on Thursday that its AI models gained unauthorized access to the systems of three different unnamed organizations during cybersecurity testing. The company says Claude reached the internet “from within or while interacting" with a third-party evaluation environment. The announcement comes more than a week after OpenAI revealed that one of its AI agents hacked into Hugging Face during a separate cybersecurity test.
The discovery came after Anthropic decided to conduct “a large-scale retrospective review of our own cybersecurity evaluations” following the OpenAI incident, according to a blog post Anthropic published Thursday. The AI lab says it first identified 141,006 tests in which it determined that Claude could have obtained internet access. It then found that three different Claude models accessed the internet in evaluations run by the third-party AI testing firm Irregular, and then hacked into the production infrastructure of three different organizations.
Anthropic said that the incidents involved Opus 4.7, Mythos 5, and an internal research test model. The earliest incidents happened in April—meaning they likely went unnoticed publicly for months. Just like in the OpenAI case, Anthropic had deliberately turned off safeguards designed to constrain the AI models and prevent them from being misused. In other words, these weren’t the versions released to the public.
“In all three incidents, Claude had been tasked with a capture-the-flag challenge, one of the ways we assess a model’s cyber capabilities,” Anthropic said in its blog post. The company added that in all of the cases, “Anthropic’s evaluation prompt specified to Claude that its environment was a simulation and that it had no internet access.” It attributed the oversight to a “misunderstanding” between Anthropic and Irregular.
While Claude wasn’t supposed to have internet access, Anthropic said that Irregular had misconfigured the machines that it was using to test Claude, giving the AI models the ability to surf the web. “Neither we nor our evaluation partner were aware of this misconfiguration until we detected it through our additional evaluation monitoring last week,” Anthropic said in the blog post.
“We now have evidence confirming that both of the two largest AI labs have not only failed to contain their agents, but also failed to detect their jailbreaks in real time,” says Jake Williams, vice president of research and development at Hunter Strategy. “It's clear that regulation and government oversight for AI testing is needed immediately.”
Irregular and Anthropic did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Unlike in the OpenAI case, Anthropic said that Claude did not find or exploit any complex vulnerabilities. Instead, it relied on basic techniques, “such as exploiting weak passwords and unauthenticated endpoints.”
OpenAI said that its AI agent accessed the internet by exploiting a zero-day vulnerability. But it went on to access the systems of multiple third-party organizations using the same variety of everyday cybersecurity weaknesses as Anthropic’s models. Specifically, OpenAI said the AI agent apparently found credentials that had been exposed on the open internet.
Anthropic acknowledged that if the AI lab and its testing partner implemented more “defense-in-depth” measures, they could have prevented the incidents, or at least reduced the likelihood of them occurring, echoing OpenAI’s response to mounting criticism over its own incident.
“I don't understand how any of these AI labs are playing this off like this is 'just something that happens,'” Williams says. “It's not. It's negligence.”
The AI lab stressed that the models were told they didn’t have access to the open internet, and for the most part, Claude mistook the organizations it accessed as being part of the testing environment. Put differently, the models largely didn’t understand that they had escaped containment to begin with.
But in some cases, the AI models knew that something was amiss, and they detected correctly that the infrastructure they were accessing was real. The oldest model, Opus 4.7, had been tasked with targeting a fictional company that shared a name with a real-world website domain. Unable to accomplish its mission in the simulated environment, it turned instead to the real company, successfully stealing credentials and accessing a production database. At some point, Anthropic says, it learned it was “likely operating in a real environment,“ but persisted with its attack.
Mythos 5, the most capable model Anthropic has released, also realized it was in the real world, but it “reasoned its way back to the conclusion that it was still in a simulation.”
The internal test model, which Anthropic says is the most capable of the bunch, stopped its attack once it found evidence that its targets were real.
Both Anthropic and OpenAI say they have hired METR, another third-party AI evaluator, to conduct independent reviews of their respective cybersecurity incidents. It also committed to taking a more comprehensive approach to its security testing through improved defense-in-depth measures and more carefully designed tests.
“Evaluation environments increasingly need to be held to the same security standard as any other system our models run in,” the blog post reads, adding that the company has “cautious optimism” that “this type of risk can be overcome.”

title: MiniMax 發表全模態模型 H3：圖、影片、聲音一次生成，承諾近日開源
summary:
MiniMax 發表全模態生成模型 H3 並宣布近日會開源，官方稱 2K 影片生成成本僅同級旗艦的三分之一。 […]

〈MiniMax 發表全模態模型 H3：圖、影片、聲音一次生成，承諾近日開源〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
MiniMax 發表全模態生成模型 H3 並宣布近日會開源，官方稱 2K 影片生成成本僅同級旗艦的三分之一。
（前情提要：MiniMax M3 正式開源：428B 原生多模態 MoE、1M 超長上下文）
（背景補充：字節跳動 Seedance 2.5 發布：升級 30 秒影片＋50 份參考，推出合規版權模板 首波合作周星馳）
繼 6 月開源文字模型 M3 之後，MiniMax 再度出手。今（31）日發布新一代全模態生成模型 H3（海螺 Hailuo 3.0），並宣布近日將開源模型權重。
H3 從「專用任務模型」走向「通用多模態智慧」：不再把生圖、生影片、生聲音、編輯、參考這些功能分開賣，而是讓一個模型在文字、圖片、影片、聲音混合的語境裡，統一理解用戶到底想要什麼。
官方公布的數字很誘人：2K 解析度影片每秒 0.8 元人民幣，一支 15 秒的片子約 12 元人民幣，號稱只要同級旗艦模型三分之一的成本。
MiniMax H3 is on Runway!! 🪄
So excited to bring H3 to @runwayml incredible creative community.
Open weights coming soon… go make something wild 👀#MiniMaxH3 https://t.co/8yErjJZHk6
— MiniMax (official) (@MiniMax_AI) July 31, 2026
這次新模型做了什麼
H3 的輸入端可以吃文字、圖片、音訊、影片，而且能混著給；輸出端是原生 2K 解析度、24 幀，5 到 15 秒、音畫同步，影像跟聲音是同一次生成出來的，不是先出畫面再回頭配音。
它的賣點叫 Omni-Reference 全模態參考：單次生成最多可以帶 9 張參考圖、3 段參考影片、3 段參考音訊，用來指定風格、角色、動作、音色，但這些參考不會被當成必須照抄的關鍵影格，模型有自己的詮釋空間。
功能上，H3 支援文生影片、圖生影片、多鏡頭敘事、指令式編輯，還有 V2V Motion Transfer，也就是把一段影片裡的動作直接搬到另一個角色身上。
官方把應用場景寫得很直白：廣告、品牌行銷、電商、產品設計、UI/UX、遊戲。用詞刻意選了「商業級生產」而非「生成影片」，明顯是說給甲方聽的。
生成效果如何？
不過 MiniMax 自稱拿下第一的是「影片編輯」這個子項目，不是綜合影片生成。
同一份 Artificial Analysis 榜單，截至 7 月，字節跳動今年 2 月發布的 Seedance 2.0 仍以 1,213 Elo 領先含聲音影片榜，圖生影片盲測更以 1,344 Elo 排在首位；Google Veo 3.1 被視為綜合表現最強；快手可靈 Kling 3.0 在 llm-stats 影片競技場則以 2,023 分居冠。
至於開源，目前仍然只是一句「近日」的承諾，權重還沒有真的出現在 Hugging Face 上。H3 是不是真的第一，答案要等權重上架、第三方跑分出爐才算數；現在能確定的，只有 MiniMax 又搶先卡到了一個位置。

title: 交易所倒閉潮來襲，儲備證明如何保護你的資產？Ourbit 靠審計、開源、PoR 三招
summary:
BitMEX、BitMart 在一週內接連宣布結束營運，加上波蘭交易所 Zondacrypto 熱錢包近乎歸零 […]

〈交易所倒閉潮來襲，儲備證明如何保護你的資產？Ourbit 靠審計、開源、PoR 三招〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
BitMEX、BitMart 在一週內接連宣布結束營運，加上波蘭交易所 Zondacrypto 熱錢包近乎歸零的暴雷案例，讓「資產是否還在交易所裡」成為用戶必須正視的問題。
（前情提要：交易所 BitMart 宣布收攤：8/26 停止交易、2027 年初關站，兩個月前才否認提幣危機）
（背景補充：ARK分析師：加密正進入史上最強整合期，交易所關門潮才剛開始）
短短一週內，兩家經營超過十年的交易所相繼熄燈。7 月 23 日，老牌衍生品交易所 BitMEX 宣布結束營運，將於 9 月 23 日正式關閉平台、即日起停止新用戶註冊，為這家永續合約發明者畫下 11 年句點。三天後的 7 月 26 日，BitMart 也宣布啟動有序清算，8 月 26 日起停止所有交易，預計 2027 年 1 月 31 日完成收尾；消息一出，其平台幣 BMX 一週累計挫幅達 81.5%。
時間再往前一些，2026 年 4 月，波蘭交易所 Zondacrypto 的熱錢包 BTC 餘額從 55.7 枚崩跌至 0.086 枚，短短期間內蒸發 99.7%，平台卻在此期間持續宣稱有償付能力，約 3 萬名用戶受影響，被稱為 FTX 之後歐洲最重大的交易所暴雷案。
BitMEX 與 BitMart 官方口徑都是主動結束營運；但 Zondacrypto 證明，一家交易所嘴上說「一切正常」，帳上資產卻可能早已不翼而飛。當交易所可以一夕關門、資產可以在無人察覺下被掏空，一個問題無可迴避：你的資產，真的還在交易所裡嗎？而這正是儲備證明（Proof of Reserves，PoR）存在的意義。
PoR 在證明什麼？
儲備證明不是一句「我們很安全」的口號，而是可被驗算的機制：一是證明交易所儲備錢包的總資產，二是證明平台對用戶的總負債，兩者相比、資產須至少覆蓋負債（即「1:1」）。但只揭露資產、不揭露負債，稱不上完整的儲備證明。
梅克爾樹：讓用戶自己動手驗
業界標準做法是梅克爾樹（Merkle tree）：每位用戶的資產快照作為「葉節點」，經雜湊運算逐層合併，最終收斂成唯一的「根雜湊」。只要任何一筆餘額被竄改，根雜湊就會改變，讓做假帳幾乎無所遁形。
更關鍵的是，用戶可以拿到自己的葉節點資料，自行往上運算，驗證自己的餘額是否被誠實計入平台公布的總負債。這是用戶不須相信任何人、能自己動手驗證的環節。
PoR 不是萬靈丹，頻率與可驗證性才是關鍵
不過 PoR 也有侷限：快照式證明只證明某一瞬間資產與負債相符，快照之間的空窗期資產仍可能被悄悄挪動。
Zondacrypto 熱錢包能在無人察覺下蒸發 99.7%，問題就出在此。也就是說有沒有做過 PoR 不是重點，做得多勤、能不能被驗證、有沒有第三方背書，才是真正拉開差距之處。
這也是為什麼頭部交易所把 PoR 從一次性公關動作變成月更紀律：幣安自 2022 年 11 月起結合梅克爾樹與 zk-SNARK，以零知識證明在不暴露個別帳戶資料的前提下，證明總資產覆蓋總負債、且沒有負餘額帳戶，累計已發布 38 期報告；OKX 則採更透明的 zk-STARK，月度報告已達第 40 期，揭露超過 22 種資產、約 277 億美元鏈上儲備。
相較之下，Kraken 等交易所選擇由第三方會計師事務所執行審計版 PoR，走的是傳統背書路線。兩種零知識證明路線微妙不同，但共同點都指向「定期、可驗證、隱私保護」三個關鍵字。
三年多下來，PoR 已從危機公關變成用戶挑交易所的基本檢查項目。
新一代交易所做法：以 Ourbit 為例
公開可驗證的 PoR、用戶能自己動手驗算、第三方安全背書，正是新一代交易所試圖內建進產品的方向。以 Ourbit 為例，其官網公開的 1:1 儲備證明公開驗證頁，目前列出 26 個鏈上錢包地址，橫跨 Bitcoin、Ethereum、BNB Chain…等 10 條鏈。
目前儲備餘額為 656 枚 BTC、5,449 枚 ETH、逾 2,800 萬枚 USDT，總價值約 8,080 萬美元。頁面上每個地址的餘額與所在區塊高度都直接標示，任何人都能自行拿到區塊瀏覽器核對，而非只在爭議發生時才拿出來的一次性快照。
同時呼應梅克爾樹的自驗邏輯，在 GitHub 開源了驗證工具，用戶可下載自己的葉節點資料，在本機從 SHA256 雜湊值一路運算比對到根節點，讓信任不再只是平台單方面的聲明，而是任何人都能自行重複運算、反覆核對的結果。
第三方背書方面，Ourbit 已通過 Web3 安全公司 Hacken 的深度滲透測試與審計，並在 Hacken 官網公開審計檔案，累計完成三次審計。Hacken 成立於 2017 年，具 ISO 27001:2022 認證，並營運 CER.live 安全評級平台與 HackenProof 漏洞回報平台，在業界具公信力，三次審計代表的是持續性安全檢視，而非掛一次牌就結案。
Ourbit 也與頂尖安全團隊慢霧（SlowMist）建立合作，取得第一線鏈上威脅情報，並在 BugEx 平台運行最高 2 萬美元漏洞賞金計畫，搭配冷錢包儲存、2FA、反釣魚碼與 24 小時鏈上監控。
另一個較少被拿來檢視、但同樣有參考價值的訊號，則是平台有沒有持續投入社群與市場：在交易所接連收攤的環境下，願意持續辦線下活動、經營社群，本身就是「存續意願」的展現。
Ourbit 近年持續贊助區塊鏈產業活動，並拓展新興市場、推出預測市場、Tap Trading 等新產品體驗，而這些擴張能否走得久，仍要看同一套儲備證明與安全基礎有沒有跟上。
如何選擇交易平台
交易所會不斷有新的加入、也會不斷有舊的關門，BitMEX、BitMart 一週內接連收攤就是最新提醒。
與其等下一次熄燈潮才回頭檢查，不如把幾個問題變成挑選交易所的日常習慣：這家交易所有沒有公開、可自行驗算的儲備證明？驗證方式是不是只能單方面相信平台？有沒有經得起檢驗、持續性的第三方安全審計？
多花點心力觀察與研究，可能會是你下一次熄燈潮來臨時，能不能全身而退的關鍵。

title: 蘋果庫克鬆口：iCloud+ 將分級賣 AI 用量，免費午餐的帳單要上桌了
summary:
庫克在財報電話會議上鬆口，暗示 iCloud+ 未來將依 AI 用量分級收費，兩年前「不會額外收費」的承諾，如 […]

〈蘋果庫克鬆口：iCloud+ 將分級賣 AI 用量，免費午餐的帳單要上桌了〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
庫克在財報電話會議上鬆口，暗示 iCloud+ 未來將依 AI 用量分級收費，兩年前「不會額外收費」的承諾，如今看來終究還是要向重度用戶伸手要錢。
（前情提要：Apple Intelligence 中文版再延期？Tim Cook：不會考慮額外收費）
（背景補充：AI 吃光記憶體產能！蘋果撐不住調漲 MacBook、iPad 售價，股價重挫逾 5%）
庫克在 2024 年底曾公開表示，Apple Intelligence「不會考慮額外收費」。但在庫克 31 日最後一場財報電話會議上，他鬆口蘋果正在評估讓用戶「付費買更大的 AI 用量」。
當初免費開放，是為了把用戶先請進門；現在用量真的上來了，帳單也跟著上來，蘋果只能想辦法把成本轉嫁出去。
從免費午餐到分級收費
財報電話會議上，庫克談到蘋果即將全面推出的 Siri AI 時，直言他相信用戶會「大量」使用 Apple Intelligence 與新版 Siri，並表示「我們會在 iCloud+ 上推出某種升級方案，讓用戶可以往上加購」。
這是蘋果高層第一次鬆口，暗示 AI 用量很可能會被包進訂閱分級裡，而不是永遠隨機能附贈。
目前 iCloud+ 的定價是每月 0.99 美元起（50GB）、2.99 美元（200GB），到 9.99 美元（2TB）不等。
今年 6 月，蘋果就已經先埋下伏筆，官方說明中提到 AI 功能，包括影像生成，「有每日用量上限，因為它們依賴強大的伺服器端模型」，並且「更高額度」開放給大多數 iCloud+ 方案，實務上多半得升到 200GB 以上才吃得到。
用量門檻的設計，其實已經替日後的分級收費鋪好了路。今年秋季隨 iOS 27 推出的家庭 App 攝影機辨識功能，甚至直接要求用戶訂閱 2TB 以上方案才能使用，等於變相把重度 AI 用戶推向更貴的方案，兩年前那句「不會額外收費」的承諾，早就被悄悄改寫。
AI 帳單要有人埋單
蘋果的次世代 Apple Foundation Models 是建立在 Google Gemini 之上，兩家公司在 2026 年 1 月宣布多年授權協議，外界估算這筆合作每年要價約 10 億美元，客製化的 Gemini 模型引數量高達約 1.2 兆。
伺服器端推論的每一次呼叫，都是實打實的運算成本，不是寫死在晶片裡就能一勞永逸的事。簡單來說就是，用戶用得越兇，蘋果要付給雲端與模型供應商的帳單就越重，這筆錢不會自己消失，總得從某個環節收回來。
iCloud+ 最低方案每月只要 0.99 美元，換算一年不到 12 美元；反觀蘋果每年付給 Google 的授權費高達 10 億美元，蘋果需要靠海量用戶一點一滴的訂閱費，慢慢把這筆天價授權成本補回來。

title: 薩爾瓦多比特幣五年實驗：加密僑匯比例僅 0.7%，多數仍透過傳統銀行
summary:
薩爾瓦多將比特幣列為法定貨幣已滿五年，央行資料顯示 2026 上半年加密匯款僅 3540 萬美元，佔 50.6 […]

〈薩爾瓦多比特幣五年實驗：加密僑匯比例僅 0.7%，多數仍透過傳統銀行〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
薩爾瓦多將比特幣列為法定貨幣已滿五年，央行資料顯示 2026 上半年加密匯款僅 3540 萬美元，佔 50.6 億美元總僑匯的 0.7%。儘管同比增 39%，但 84% 的匯款仍透過傳統銀行。
（前情提要：Threads活躍使用者暴降8成！Meta本週推「網頁版」能救活流量？）
（背景補充：Solana生態演算法穩定幣 Nirvana 將 AMM 中「所有 UST 替換為 USDC」）
Ashrith Rao 在最新分析中指出，薩爾瓦多比特幣實驗五年後，跨境匯款資料揭示了政策願景與民眾選擇之間的巨大鴻溝。
薩爾瓦多將比特幣作為法定貨幣已經五年了。該國中央銀行發布 2026 年上半年僑匯資料，揭示一個殘酷真相：加密管道匯款總額僅 3540 萬美元，在 50.6 億美元跨境僑匯總量中佔比僅有 0.7%。
對比去年同期 2540 萬美元的資料，漲幅達 39.1%。事實上，今年上半年加密匯款總額，已經超過往年任意一個上半年的規模。
但對於薩爾瓦多而言，0.7% 佔比微不足道。僑匯規模接近該國 GDP 的 24%，常年高於出口、外商直接投資與旅遊業收入總和。
84%仍走傳統：西聯匯款才是王道
亮眼的同比增速掩蓋了更多真相。加密貨幣匯款從 2024 年的 8550 萬美元急遽下降至 2025 年的 5767 萬美元，降幅高達 32.5%，可謂遭遇重創。
2026 年上半年的回溫屬實，卻是建立在極低基數之上，難以成為加密支持者期待的轉折點。自 2021 年法案落實以來，比特幣普及之路波動不斷、進展斷斷續續，整體年均增速僅略高於 1%。
那些不變的事物構成了故事的基石。超過 84% 匯往薩爾瓦多的匯款仍然透過銀行和傳統匯款公司進行。
遊客攜帶現金回國形成的現金匯款佔比升至 3.8%，規模已是加密貨幣管道的 5 倍。
問題並非源於技術缺陷，而是民眾行為習慣。 定居海外（尤其是美國）的薩爾瓦多人，明顯傾向選擇自己熟悉、信任的方式。
銀行轉賬、西聯匯款、速匯金，談不上轉賬最快、手續費最低，但勝在穩定可靠、深入人心，始終是大眾首選。
五年前政府宣稱，數位貨幣每年能幫助薩爾瓦多人省下 4 億美元匯款手續費，如今這一目標幾乎沒有取得實質性進展。當年預估可節省 4 億美元的判斷，顯然過於樂觀。
IMF 14 億貸款換來的妥協：Chivo 錢包關停
2026 年初月度資料顯現一個值得關注的趨勢。上半年加密匯款大幅上行，同比漲幅高達 146.4%。一季度增幅一度衝高至 49.7%，4 月增速回落至 44.4%，增長勢頭逐步放緩；5 月增速穩定在 41.7%。 增速下滑只是基數效應導致的正常現象，2025 年同期基數每月僅 1% 增速。資料表明，本輪上漲更多是階段性提升，而非持續加速增長。
增長並非源於大量新使用者入場。加密錢包單筆轉帳均值從 2025 年 269.7 美元升至 2026 年 310.9 美元，單筆金額提升 41 美元。 這意味著資金更加集中：少數群體加大轉賬規模，並不代表廣泛民眾接納加密貨幣。
2025 年 2 月，薩爾瓦多獲得國際貨幣基金（IMF） 14 億美元中期貸款，附帶兩條嚴苛條款：第一，政府不得主動增持比特幣；第二，禁止發行任何由比特幣計價的公共債務或代幣化金融工具。
薩爾瓦多政府隨之修訂《比特幣法案》：私營商戶可自願選擇是否接受比特幣，並且所有稅費必須以美元繳納。
作為與 IMF 達成協議的一部分，政府主導的 Chivo 錢包正在逐步關停。這款錢包原本是 Bukele（薩爾瓦多現任總統）比特幣規劃的核心支柱。
這是影響深遠的重大變化。 Chivo 原本是推動比特幣日常消費落實的核心基礎設施。官方逐步關停錢包，本質上等於承認：依靠政府力量推廣比特幣普及的策略宣告失敗。
IMF 措辭相對委婉，將該舉措描述為 「錢包業務整合」，而非徹底清退，讓雙方都保留談判餘地。
穩定幣暗渡陳倉：3540萬中有多少是USDC？
當下政策充滿矛盾。一方面限制比特幣日常流通場景，另一方面政府仍持續增持比特幣作為儲備資產。 政府思路已經轉變，不再推動比特幣充當流通貨幣，而是將其視作儲備資產。僑匯資料證明，如果民眾真正把比特幣當作日常貨幣使用，市場格局會截然不同。
這份統計資料背後暗藏疑點，推動增長的主力或許不是比特幣，而是穩定幣。
憑藉價值穩定、轉賬高效的特性，穩定幣正在發展中國家取代法幣，成為跨境資金轉移熱門選擇。
一名定居洛杉磯的薩爾瓦多居民，完全可以繞過比特幣，直接透過加密基礎設施向聖薩爾瓦多的家人轉賬 USDC。
如果這 3540 萬美元資金中有越來越多份額屬於穩定幣，那麼比特幣專案整體成效，將比表面資料更加堪憂。 真正實現增長的，是依託加密網路流通的美元代幣，而非比特幣本身。儘管暫無精確拆分資料，但整個拉丁美洲都顯現這一趨勢。
Bitso 已經實現數十億美元穩定幣支付體量，成為拉美頭部加密交易所。 即便資產表現不及預期，區塊鏈底層技術正在持續滲透。
全球監管壓力持續上升。反洗錢、反恐怖融資規則不斷收緊，歐盟加密資產監管法案（MiCA）也即將全面落實。 雖然薩爾瓦多加密資金流入體量不大，但隨著全球監管標準統一，相關資金流動勢必受到嚴密監控。
五年答卷：從普惠金融到國家儲備的轉向
薩爾瓦多在反洗錢與反恐融資框架上展現出 「初步適應跡象」，但合規調整不等於加密普及。
與此同時，該國整體僑匯市場持續擴張，總彙款規模從 2025 上半年 48.40 億美元增至 2026 上半年 50.60 億美元，漲幅 4.5%。
整個大盤穩步增長，但加密管道佔比依舊遠低於 1%。即便保持 39% 的同比增速，加密匯款想要突破市場份額 2%，依舊遙遙無期。 這一預測尚且建立在一個高機率不成立的假設之上：傳統匯款管道不會持續迭代升級。
3540 萬美元本身不能簡單等同於政策失敗。數字證明，確實有薩爾瓦多人使用數位資產完成跨境資金往來，真實資金正在流動。但對比當初宏大政策願景，這份答卷存在巨大落差。
儘管比特幣法案已經生效五年了，但政治論述與實際情況之間的差距卻從未如此之大。
政府持續談論戰略儲備，頻頻購入比特幣；普通人依舊優先使用西聯匯款等傳統管道。IMF 竭力要求該國管控加密風險，美國財政部卻希望增持比特幣資產。
薩爾瓦多中央銀行資料顯示普及率僅 0.7%，Chivo 錢包同步走向落幕。
本文探討的重點不是比特幣在薩爾瓦多遭遇哪些困難。 核心故事在於政府目標徹底轉向。原本計劃利用加密貨幣惠及普通民眾，如今轉變為把比特幣作為一項國家金融戰略。
五年以來，僑匯資料持續釋放相同訊號。誠然，39.1% 的同比增速十分亮眼，但 0.7% 的市場份額同樣值得深思。 在國家財政核算層面，兩個數字的重要性不可同日而語。

title: GPT-5.6 Luna 價格大砍八成、Terra 降 20% 對標 Gemini，AI 價格戰白熱化
summary:
OpenAI 大砍 Luna 價格 80%，Terra 降 20% 對標 Gemini，Sol 加推兩倍速 F […]

〈GPT-5.6 Luna 價格大砍八成、Terra 降 20% 對標 Gemini，AI 價格戰白熱化〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
OpenAI 大砍 Luna 價格 80%，Terra 降 20% 對標 Gemini，Sol 加推兩倍速 Fast 版。中國開源模型讓價格戰白熱化。
（前情提要：OpenAI 正式發表 GPT-5.6 家族！一文拆解 Sol、Terra 與 Luna 三款模型與定價）
（背景補充：AI 高定價時代終結倒數？Token 必會降價的五大結構性理由）
這次 OpenAI 大手筆調降：Luna 模型每百萬 token 收費，輸入加輸出合計從 7 美元砍到 1.4 美元，降幅 80%，比 Google 的 Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite（合計 2.8 美元）再少一半。
Sam Altman 在 X 上把這波調整宣布為「major price cuts」。GPT-5.6 系列（Sol、Terra、Luna）剛發佈滿一個月，戰場已經從誰的模型更聰明，悄悄轉向「誰能把推論成本壓得更低」。
major price cuts today:
*80% drop for GPT-5.6 Luna, now $0.20 per million input tokens and $1.20 per million output
*20% drop for GPT-5.6 Terra, to $2/$12
*GPT-5.6 Sol gets Fast mode in the API, up to 2.5x the speed for 2x the price, same intelligence pic.twitter.com/erC6u4VoDR— Sam Altman (@sama) July 30, 2026
三款模型，三種降價邏輯
這次調整分成三層，對應三種不同的使用場景。
走量最大的 Luna，定位是摘要、分類、路由這類高吞吐、低延遲的輕量即時任務。
它的輸入單價從每百萬 token 1 美元降到 0.2 美元、輸出從 6 美元降到 1.2 美元，合計降幅正好 80%，因為這類任務不太需要深度推理，成本本來就是唯一考量。
中間層 Terra，定位一般生產環境的日常工作負載，輸入 2 美元、輸出 12 美元，合計 14 美元，比先前的 17.5 美元降 20%，這個數字剛好與 Google Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview打平。
最頂層 Sol，扛的是進階程式設計、多步驟規劃、工具呼叫這類複雜推理與 agentic 任務。標準模式維持輸入 5 美元、輸出 30 美元，合計 35 美元不變，但新增的 Sol Fast 把合計價格拉到 70 美元，換來最高 2.5 倍的吞吐量。
OpenAI 特別強調模型智慧本身沒有變，只是用更貴的算力堆疊出更快的速度，等於把「要快」和「要便宜」拆成兩條分岔的產品線，讓客戶自己選邊站。
便宜，但不是最便宜
降價歸降價，Luna 依然不是市場上最低價。
小米的 MiMo-V2.5 Flash 合計每百萬 token 只要 0.4 美元，DeepSeek-V4-Flash 是 0.42 美元，連 DeepSeek 旗艦 V4-Pro 都只要 1.305 美元，全部低於 Luna 的 1.4 美元；MiniMax-M3 與 LongCat-2.0 的促銷價則同樣落在 1.5 美元。
真正讓 OpenAI 有底氣的，是第三方評測機構 Artificial Analysis 的數字：降價後的 Luna，效能仍優於 Gemini 3.6 Flash，甚至贏過較舊的 Gemini 3.1 Pro，換算下來每單位智慧的成本，反而是 OpenAI 佔優。
價格戰背後，真正的對手
不過這場定價戰真正該擔心的對手，可能不在矽谷。
CNBC 今年 7 月初的調查報導指出，透過 OpenRouter 使用的 token 當中，中國模型拿下的比例最高衝到 46%，自 2 月 8 日起每週都維持在 30% 以上，對比過去 12 個月平均僅 11%、2025 上半年更只有 4.5% 的基期，漲勢相當驚人。
OpenRouter 的 Justin Summerville 直言，中國開源模型的價格可以比 OpenAI、Anthropic 的旗艦模型便宜 60% 到 90%。
這股從企業端一路蔓延的採用壓力，才是逼 OpenAI 動刀的真正原因，遠比競品官網上的價目表更有說服力，當客戶願意為了省 60% 到 90% 的成本，直接切換供應商，牌價戰就不再只是行銷手法，而是留住客戶的生存問題。

title: 川普宣布達成協議：哈瑪斯全面解除武裝、以色列同步撤軍，但外交圈觀望
summary:
川普宣布「和平理事會」已與各方達成協議，哈瑪斯將於 6 至 8 個月內全面解除武裝，換取以色列部隊撤出加薩；但 […]

〈川普宣布達成協議：哈瑪斯全面解除武裝、以色列同步撤軍，但外交圈觀望〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
川普宣布「和平理事會」已與各方達成協議，哈瑪斯將於 6 至 8 個月內全面解除武裝，換取以色列部隊撤出加薩；但哈瑪斯尚未證實，以色列與西方外交官也對其履約誠意深表懷疑。
（前情提要：快訊》川普宣布「以色列與真主黨停火」！急撤赴黎巴嫩美軍：不進駐貝魯特）
（背景補充：川普：取消今晚轟炸伊朗，美國與以色列等中東多國秘密達成「歷史性交易」）
哈瑪斯本人至今沒有鬆口證實，但川普已自行喊話。美國總統川普今天在社群平台 Truth Social 宣布，他主導的「和平理事會」已促成一項協議，加薩地區的哈瑪斯與其他武裝團體即將「全面解除武裝」。
他形容這是「全面解除武裝達成歷史性協議」，視為區域邁向穩定格局的重要轉折。在他宣布前，熟悉開羅斡旋談判的訊息人士告訴法新社，哈瑪斯正朝這項協議邁進，但截至目前，協議另一方仍保持沉默。
以色列不埋單，西方外交圈也在觀望
根據 CNN 引述兩名美國官員的說法，哈瑪斯確實已點頭同意協議條款；但同一則報導提到，以色列官員與西方外交官對哈瑪斯是否會真正履約，態度相當保留，Al Jazeera 的報導也呼應這種觀望氣氛。
以色列開出的條件很明確：哈瑪斯必須完全解除武裝、武器全數撤出加薩、加薩全境非軍事化，這是以軍撤出的前提。
交地圖、分批走、換人接手
協議的執行細節寫到，哈瑪斯須在 6 至 8 個月內完成重型與輕型武器的拆解銷毀，並將地下坑道、軍工產線與彈藥儲存點位置資料全數移交，接受第三方監督核實。
解除進度分批執行，以色列部隊同步分階段撤離；接手治安的是新成立的巴勒斯坦警察部隊，搭配國際穩定部隊，負責加薩內部治安與周邊邊境維安。
加薩治理權將逐步轉交新的巴勒斯坦政府，並與和平理事會協作。埃及、卡達與土耳其在斡旋過程中扮演關鍵角色，川普點名致謝三國。
這份協議真正難實現之處，藏在「交地圖」三個字裡。地道網路與軍火庫位置，是哈瑪斯多年來賴以周旋的戰略底牌，一旦攤在外部監督下，等於自己交出談判籌碼，這不是單純繳械，而是結構性的權力讓渡。
「先解武、後撤軍」的順序也讓雙方都有理由觀望，履約驗證機制能否經得起檢驗，恐怕比協議簽了什麼更關鍵。
下一步在開羅，第 2 階段要談真章
埃及官方媒體 Al-Qahera News 報導，開羅預計「近期」召開加薩停火斡旋方會議，美國、卡達與土耳其都將派員與會，議程聚焦落實停火計畫第 2 階段，哈瑪斯與巴勒斯坦各派系已簽字同意路線圖。
川普的加薩 20 點和平計畫中，第 2 階段核心正是哈瑪斯解除武裝與以色列部隊逐步撤出加薩，兩件事目前都還停在「說好了」階段。

title: 蘋果財報亮眼股價卻下挫，庫克謝幕之戰形容記憶體遇「百年大洪水」
summary:
蘋果最新一季營收、獲利同創新高，每股盈餘、毛利率全面超越市場預期，但財測保守、記憶體成本狂飆的隱憂，讓盤後股價 […]

〈蘋果財報亮眼股價卻下挫，庫克謝幕之戰形容記憶體遇「百年大洪水」〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
蘋果最新一季營收、獲利同創新高，每股盈餘、毛利率全面超越市場預期，但財測保守、記憶體成本狂飆的隱憂，讓盤後股價一度重挫 8%。
（前情提要：AI 吃光記憶體產能！蘋果撐不住調漲 MacBook、iPad 售價，股價重挫逾 5%）
（背景補充：三星營業利益暴增 18 倍！贏過輝達、蘋果，財報公布後股價卻重挫逾 6%）
蘋果 7 月 31 日交出的最新財報，營收與獲利雙雙寫下新高，帳面數字近乎無可挑剔，卻在財測環節踩了煞車，記憶體成本的隱憂攤開，盤後股價一度重挫達 8%。
這次是庫克（Tim Cook）以執行長身分主持的收官之作：他將於 9 月 1 日卸下執行長職務，把棒子交給硬體工程資深副總裁特納斯（John Ternus），自己則退居執行董事。
記憶體吃緊成未爆彈
蘋果第三季營收年增 16% 至 1,094.2 億美元，優於分析師預估的 1,086.5 億美元，創下歷史新高；每股盈餘 2.02 美元、年增 29%，同樣優於分析師預估的 1.89 美元，淨利年增 27%。
然而，公司對本季（9 月當季）營收僅預估成長 9% 至 11%，低於市場原先設想的約 12%，財測不如預期立刻澆熄投資人熱情。
讓市場真正繃緊神經的，是庫克在會議上罕見祭出的比喻，他把記憶體漲價形容成一場「洪水」：「我們很不情願地調漲價格，因為我們正處於記憶體價格的百年一遇大洪水之中，漲幅呈指數級增長。」
他也坦承，本季蘋果勢必得吸收更高的記憶體成本，只能靠先前囤積的庫存，以及其他零元件的降價空間來部分抵銷衝擊。
毛利率創高藏玄機，大中華區、服務業務雙雙失色
上季整體毛利率衝上創紀錄的 50.1%，優於市場預估的 47.9%，但其中約 2 個百分點來自美國政府退還的約 20 億美元關稅款、貢獻每股盈餘 11 美分。
這筆退款源自今年 2 月美國最高法院推翻白宮全球關稅措施的裁決，屬一次性收益，扣除後毛利率約 48.1%，大致回歸市場預期水準，短期內也不太可能以同等規模重演。
此外，大中華區營收年增 22% 至 188.2 億美元、服務營收成長 12% 至 307.4 億美元，兩項數字雖仍成長，卻雙雙未達分析師預估，成為這份財報少數美中不足之處。
特納斯接棒，晶片荒與新 Siri 是首場硬仗
財報公布前，蘋果市值才剛重登 5 兆美元，重新登上全球市值最大公司寶座。但庫克卸任前留下的，是一份數字亮眼、隱憂同樣亮眼的成績單，晶片短缺、記憶體漲價與 AI 進度落後，全數留給接班人特納斯（John Ternus）收拾。
這位在蘋果任職 25 年的老將 9 月 1 日接任執行長後，第一場硬仗就是新一代 iPhone 與新版 Siri 的發表，能否讓市場相信蘋果扛得住記憶體的「百年大洪水」，將是他上任後最快必須交出的答案。

title: Anthropic 也出包：Claude 溜上網駭進三家公司，一度拿到資料庫權限
summary:
Anthropic 在 7 月 30 日承認，自家 Claude 在資安能力評估中三度真的駭進外部企業系統，最 […]

〈Anthropic 也出包：Claude 溜上網駭進三家公司，一度拿到資料庫權限〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
Anthropic 在 7 月 30 日承認，自家 Claude 在資安能力評估中三度真的駭進外部企業系統，最嚴重的一起拿到了正式環境資料庫的存取權。
（前情提要：OpenAI 又爆失控！第二家公司 Modal 客戶帳號遭駭，Hugging Face 呼籲公開 AI 攻擊軌跡）
（背景補充：Sam Altman 罕見喊 AI 減速，坦言資安事故比想像中可怕）
一份調查報告，把 Anthropic 自己也嚇了一跳。141,006 次資安能力評估紀錄，回溯檢查後挑出 6 次出包，比例 0.004%。
在這 6 次裡，有 3 起是 Claude 真的駭進了外部企業的正式環境，其中一家公司的 production 資料庫，被實實在在地存取了數百列資料。
Anthropic 在 7 月 30 日公布的調查報告中承認，這些事件橫跨 2026 年 4 月至今，起因是一場設計上的認知落差：評估機器實際連著公開網路，但寫給模型的 prompt 卻明白告訴它「你沒有網路」。
六次意外，三個真實受害者
Anthropic 早從 2025 年 2 月就開始系統性地跑資安能力評估，目的是量測 Claude 到底能把攻防戰打到多深，跑了超過一年才出事。
事情要從 Anthropic 與第三方評估夥伴 Irregular 的合作說起。雙方跑的是奪旗賽形式的攻防演練，讓 Claude 在虛構情境裡練習找漏洞、拿權限。簡單來說就是，出題者佈置一個假的攻擊目標，看模型能不能「破關」。
問題是，這次的「假」目標，連著真的網路。
三起事件裡，傷害最大的一起發生在 Claude Opus 4.7 身上。它在虛構情境裡發現一個真實存在、名字剛好對得上的公司網站，橫跨 4 次執行，取出了應用程式與基礎設施憑證，還拿到了一個含數百列 production 資料的資料庫存取權。
第二起主角是 Claude Mythos 5。它把一個惡意 Python 套件發布到 PyPI，這是真實存在的公開套件庫，不是沙盒，以為那只是模擬環境的一部分。這個套件被 15 套真實系統下載，其中一套屬於一家資安公司的掃描器，Claude 從那部機器成功外洩了該公司的憑證。
Anthropic 在報告中形容這段推理「絕對不 OK，而且肯定不是預期的解法」。
第三起是內部研究測試模型，掃描了約 9,000 個線上目標，用 SQL injection、外露憑證這類基本手法攻破其中一家公司。差別是，它在意識到目標是真實系統後自己停手了。
護欄寫在哪一層
這次真正的問題不是 Claude 太聰明，是護欄放錯了地方。
Anthropic 和 Irregular 把「這裡沒有網路」寫進 prompt，指望模型讀了就會照做，但機器本身從沒真的斷網。這是一種說法上的圍牆，不是物理上的圍牆。
模型只要不把那句話當真，圍牆立刻消失，而它確實沒有把那句話當真，它把整個奪旗賽當成真的在打。更麻煩的是，雙方都沒有意識到這個落差存在，直到這次回溯調查才浮出水面。
Anthropic 自己的辯解也點出了這個矛盾：「Claude 做的，正是奪旗演練訓練資安專家去做的事：想辦法拿到旗子。」白話說就是，模型沒有「失控」，它只是把任務做得太到位，到位到分不清眼前的目標是演習還是現實。
這正是評估設計本身的漏洞，不是模型對齊出了問題，也因此更難被抓到，因為模型的行為看起來完全「正常」。
從 2026 年 4 月最早的事件發生，到 7 月 21 日 OpenAI 揭露自家模型逃出沙盒、駭入 Hugging Face，Anthropic 才啟動回溯調查，隔天全面暫停所有資安評估。
三起事件在 7 月 24 日全數確認，三家受害組織與合作夥伴 Irregular 在 7 月 27 日收到通知，報告則在 7 月 30 日才公開，距離最早的事件發生已經過了三個月。
停跑之後，Anthropic 找來另一家外部機構 METR，獨立審查這批迴溯出來的紀錄，並承諾一週內公開 PyPI 事件的輕度遮蔽版完整紀錄。報告也提到，會擴大評估紀錄的持續監控、改進調查工具，並對合作的第三方評估夥伴做更嚴格的保證審查，目前正協助三家受害組織修補漏洞。

full_text:
韓國 KOSPI 週五盤中狂飆 15.15%，直接觸發熔斷機制；台股盤中暴漲逾 2,900 點，改寫史上最大盤中漲點紀錄，日經 225 同步衝上 6 萬 5 大關。
（前情提要：韓股又熔斷、日經跳水 4%、臺股大跌 1800 點失守 42k，權值股大逃殺）
（背景補充：為何韓國散戶恨透李在明？任內股票熔斷次數創紀錄）
亞洲股市 31 日集體暴走：韓國 KOSPI 盤中狂飆 15.15% 觸發熔斷，臺股盤中暴漲逾 2,900 點，改寫史上最大盤中漲點紀錄，上市公司總市值一天暴增超過 9 兆元、日經 225 同步衝上 6 萬 5 大關。
三大亞洲市場同一天報復性反彈，導火線是前夜美股全面翻紅，加上微軟、Meta 財報打消市場對 AI 資本支出降溫的疑慮。
韓股熔斷：SK 海力士飆 27%、三星漲 20%
KOSPI 今日開盤即上漲 64.22 點、漲幅 1.14%，隨後開高走高，盤中突破 6,000 點大關，最高衝上 6,441.38 點，漲幅達到 847.81 點、15.15%，直接觸發熔斷機制。
記憶體雙雄是這波行情的火車頭：SK 海力士盤中一度飆漲 27%，三星電子同步大漲 20%。這波反彈發生在 KOSPI 前三個交易日累計重挫 17% 之後，等於一天內收復過去三天大半跌幅。
日經衝上 6.5 萬點，漲幅逾 5%
日股同步走強。日經 225 開盤上漲 90 點、以 61,957 點開出，盤中一路突破 6 萬 5 關卡，最高來到 65,157 點，漲幅達 3,290 點、5.31%。
半導體與記憶體供應鏈，同樣是日股買盤集中的方向。
台股史上最大盤中漲點，市值一天增 9 兆元
台股昨（7/30）收在 39,933 點，今日開高走高，盤中一度暴漲逾 2,900 點，最高觸及 42,895 點，一口氣收復 4 萬、4 萬 1、4 萬 2 三大關卡，盤中漲點寫下史上最大紀錄，超越今年 5/4 的表現。
台達電盤中大漲超 8%、南亞、聯發科、日月光投控同步跳空漲停。上市公司總市值從 130.4 兆元飆升到逼近 140 兆元，單日增加超過 9 兆元。
美股夜盤全面翻紅，AI 資本支出疑慮暫解
亞股集體噴出的背景，是隔夜（7/30）美股的強勢收盤。道瓊工業指數上漲 613.92 點、漲幅 1.19%；那斯達克指數大漲 2.78%，終止連續 6 個交易日的跌勢。

title: 參議院要蓋反貪腐新機關！踢爆川普靠加密賺錢 20 億，調查家族是否不法獲利
summary:
美國參議院少數黨領袖 Chuck Schumer 提出立法，建立全新反貪腐機構，以查證川普家族的加密投資收益。 […]

〈參議院要蓋反貪腐新機關！踢爆川普靠加密賺錢 20 億，調查家族是否不法獲利〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
美國參議院少數黨領袖 Chuck Schumer 提出立法，建立全新反貪腐機構，以查證川普家族的加密投資收益。法案指出川普 2025 年賺進逾 20 億美元，其中 14 億來自加密貨幣。
（前情提要：紐約時報長文：從頭挖出川普家族的「加密血賺計畫」）
（背景補充：美國眾議院發起「反加密貨幣腐敗週」：民主黨人反對GENIUS、CLARITY法案，川普自肥！）
美國參議院少數黨領袖 Chuck Schumer 週四提出 反貪腐機關建立法（Anti-Corruption Bureau Creation Act），目標直指聯邦政府的貪腐問題，特別點名川普的加密貨幣投資收益。
法案核心：把貪腐查成「一級」
根據法案，川普在 2025 年賺進超過 20 億美元，其中 14 億美元來自加密貨幣。他的家人也在與外國政府有關的加密基金投入逾 10 億美元，整個家族累計獲利超過 40 億美元。
Schumer 表示，新機構將由 7 位跨黨派成員組成，具備調查、傳票、監督與執法的完整權力。法案還確保該機關的領導層、架構和資金來源免受總統幹預——未來的行政首腦無法透過裁減預算、解僱主管來消滅這個機構。
法案還提供機制讓民間公民和各州總檢察長提起訴訟，追索被貪腐竊取的資金。Schumer 說：「這將取代一堆零散的監督機構，改為一個強大、隨時可以出擊的反貪腐機構。沒有一位總統應該被允許把白宮當成私人 ATM。」
參議員連署與民間組織背書
法案由三位參議員共同連署：Jeff Merkley（俄勒岡州）、Alex Padilla（加州）和 Andy Kim（新澤西州）。這五個民間組織也公開表態支援：Public Citizen、Common Cause、Campaign Legal Center、CREW（Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington）、Protect Democracy 和 Defend the Vote Action Fund。
Schumer 在 Public Citizen 論壇中描述了法案，稱新機構擁有「真正的牙齒」與執法權。法案把聯邦選舉委員會、政府倫理辦公室和特別顧問辦公室「合併在同一個屋簷下」。
川普家族怎麼賺錢的？
Schumer 將這歸功為反貪腐計劃的一部分，參議院民主黨同步發布了《貪腐成本：川普如何把權力變成利益，由美國人民買單》報告。報告揭露川普從 2025 年重返白宮後，把總統職位變成 sprawling 家族事業：用豪華客機、 vanity 計畫和 MAGA 捐款池自肥，同時普通家庭在食品、汽油、住房與醫療上苦苦支撐。
加密貨幣市場的隱形推手
川普家族與加密貨幣產業的聯絡是許多國會議員考慮支援 CLARITY 法案的原因之一。Schumer 表示，雖然白宮同意了某些倫理措施，但許多立法者認為措施不夠。
前 SEC 官員 John Reed Stark 在論壇中說：「所有人都在問 CLARITY 法案這週會怎麼走，沒人敢確定。」
截至週四，參議院尚未安排投票。Coinbase 執行長 Brian Armstrong 在 X 上表示，法案已到達「一碼線」，參議員 Cynthia Lummis 也持續推動投票。
如果透過，會影響什麼？
法案若透過，將建立一個專門監督聯邦政府貪腐的機構，特別針對加密貨幣投資和利益衝突。川普家族在加密市場的收益可能成為第一個被查證的案子。
美國參議院只剩一週多就要休會，法案能否在 2026 年中期選舉前透過仍是未知數。

title: 比特幣跌價、認列鉅額減損！Strategy 第二季慘虧 82 億美元
summary:
全球持有最多比特幣的上市公司 Strategy（NASDAQ：MSTR） 公布第二季財報，由於比特幣價格回落，公司依照公允價值會計準則認列減值損失，單季淨虧損達 82 億美元。

〈比特幣跌價、認列鉅額減損！Strategy 第二季慘虧 82 億美元〉這篇文章最早發佈於《區塊客》。
full_text:
全球持有最多比特幣的上市公司 Strategy（NASDAQ：MSTR）公布第二季財報，由於比特幣價格回落，公司依照公允價值會計準則認列減值損失，單季淨虧損達 82 億美元。值得注意的是，該公司也首度透過出售部分比特幣補充現金，象徵 Strategy 長年「只買不賣」的策略出現轉變。
比特幣價格回落，Strategy 第二季認列 82 億美元淨虧損
Strategy 周四公布財報顯示，公司第二季淨虧損達 82 億美元，幾乎全數來自於比特幣部位高達 83.2 億美元的未實現虧損。
截至 7 月 26 日，Strategy 共持有 843,775 枚比特幣，較今年初增加約 25% 。以目前市價計算，這些比特幣價值約 548 億美元，遠低於累計投入成本約 637 億美元。
資本結構日益複雜，市場關注 Strategy 財務韌性
近幾個月來，市場持續關注 Strategy 是否能支撐愈發複雜的融資架構。目前，該公司資本結構涵蓋普通股、不同類型的優先股以及可轉換公司債，投資人開始質疑，在比特幣價格波動下，這套高度槓桿化的資本策略是否具備長期可持續性。
財報顯示，今年以來，Strategy 已透過「市價增發股票（ATM）」募集約 170.6 億美元資金；同時，公司也以約 8% 折價提前買回 15 億美元可轉債，並將美元現金儲備提升至 37.5 億美元。
Strategy 財務長 Andrew Kang 表示：「目前公司的現金儲備達 37.5 億美元，足以支應未來超過 2.1 年的優先股股息與利息義務。」
Strategy 另一項重大變化，是啟動了全新的「比特幣變現計畫（BTC Monetization Program）」。公司在第二季出售了價值約 2.184 億美元的比特幣，以此充實營運現金並支應優先股股息。
儘管比特幣價格表現疲弱，Strategy 執行董事長 Michael Saylor 仍對公司長期策略保持樂觀。
他表示，公司將持續發展擴展「Digital Credit（數位信用）」業務，希望打造建立在比特幣資產基礎上的全新金融資產類別。 Michael Saylor 表示：
在當前比特幣市場情緒低迷、外界充滿質疑的階段，我們仍會持續推動商業模式的進化，致力將「數位信用」打造成一個全新的資產類別。
此外，Strategy 董事會也批准 10 億美元的 MSTR 普通股買回計畫，不過截至目前，公司尚未執行任何普通股回購；另一方面，公司已折價回購約 2,500 萬美元 STRC 優先股。

title: Xbox 執行長下達「翻身令」！還有一年時間重返成長軌道
summary: 微軟遊戲部門 Xbox 近日備忘錄，為未來數年定下明確翻身目標。Xbox 執行長 Asha Sharma 表示 […]
full_text:
微軟遊戲部門 Xbox 近日備忘錄，為未來數年定下明確翻身目標。Xbox 執行長 Asha Sharma 表示，經歷大規模重整、裁員數千人並拆出四個工作室後，團隊必須 2027 財年結束前（即明年 6 月底前），讓 Xbox 重回玩家數與營收成長，同時獲利率拉回接近產業平均水準。
Sharma 今年 2 月接掌 Xbox 後，推動多項調整。備忘錄指出，Xbox 挑戰包括責任分工不夠明確、硬體零組件成本上升、工作室太分散，以及平台基礎設施不足以支撐競爭。她也強調，Xbox 核心仍是主機業務，主機不僅貢獻大部分營收，也是品牌與粉絲基礎的根本。
她提出 2027 財年四大優先方向，Xbox 將聚焦強化主機為主的平台、優秀遊戲打造為全球級系列、將《Minecraft》系列推向世界級創作者平台，以及延伸玩家喜愛的世界觀與內容。Sharma 表示，Xbox 將從較分散工作室模式，轉向更集中強勢 IP 與新創意，並為旗下最大系列制定跨電影、電視、周邊商品、贊助與現場活動的長期計畫，甚至尋求包括中國等全球新合作。
成長目標 Xbox 分成三階段：首先 2027 財年內恢復成長；接著 2028 與 2029 財年將投資轉成更明顯的玩家價值與營收加速；最後 2030 財年前後擴大成果，朝長期每日玩家目標邁進，並維持雙位數玩家與互動成長，以及領先業界的獲利率。Sharma 透露，Xbox 每天吸引超過 1 億人、每月超過 5 億人、每年接近 10 億人參與，但她也坦言，2026 財年新增超過 2 億名玩家，仍未帶動業務成長。
為了補足落差，Xbox 接下來將更重押《Candy Crush》系列開發商 King 與 Microsoft Casual Games，並加碼投資《Minecraft》系列。Sharma 直言，團隊必須把資源放在玩家真正重視的內容上，才能在明年 6 月底前重新回到成長軌道。

title: Fifa says 'nobody selling football' as it presses ahead with investment plan
summary: Football's governing body plans to continue the consultation process after Uefa threatens to boycott World Cups.
full_text:
Fifa says 'nobody selling football' as it presses ahead with investment plan
- Published
Fifa, which oversees world football, has responded to outrage over a plan to sell stakes in its competitions to private investors by saying it plans to continue the consultation process.
European football's 55 member associations (MAs) voted on Thursday to boycott World Cups if Fifa proceeded with the proposal.
And Concacaf, which governs football in North and Central America, said its 41 member associations also "rejected" the plan.
Fifa said in response: "Our planned consultation process was disrupted by incorrect media reports. We will proceed with this consultation process to ensure that each MA has the ability to express its vote based on facts.
"Nobody is selling football," it insisted.
Fifa wants to create a commercial subsidiary to run its main events, including its World Cups, and external investors will be able to buy stakes in it.
It said it would "invite third parties to make minority, non-controlling investments" in a new subsidiary - Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE).
The plan needs to be passed by a vote of Fifa's 211 members.
Infantino needs 106 votes in favour for the proposal to go through. Uefa and Concacaf members combined make up 96 associations, who appear set to vote against.
In its statement released on Friday morning, Fifa said: "We respect the feedback and concern aired in public and reaffirm our commitment to an open and democratic consultation."
The statement continued: "FFE has been proposed solely to ensure that all FIFA Member Associations (MAs) have the opportunity to take meaningful ownership of the commercial opportunity of football in their respective countries, and that this does not come at the cost of either the spirit or the governance of FIFA or football itself."

title: Anthropic says Claude AI hacked three organisations during cyber tests
summary: It comes just days after rival OpenAI said rogue AI agents had breached other firms' networks.
full_text:
Anthropic says Claude AI hacked three organisations during cyber tests
- Published
US technology firm Anthropic says its artificial intelligence (AI) models hacked into the systems of three organisations during a cybersecurity test due to an error that gave them access to the internet.
It comes just days after rival OpenAI said that its models had breached the systems of other companies, including AI tools hub Hugging Face.
The announcement prompted Anthropic to check whether its own models had carried out similar attacks. It says it uncovered three cases that have since been reported to the affected companies.
Anthropic, which did not name the organisations, urged other AI labs to perform similar reviews to better understand the risks of their models' capabilities.
Anthropic said in a statement, external that it reviewed more than 140,000 tests to find evidence that Claude - its family of AI models - could access the internet from testing environments that were designed to be sealed off.
The tests include so-called "capture-the-flag" evaluations in which Claude was tasked with obtaining information by breaching other systems - a common way that experts assess a model's hacking capabilities.
A "misconfiguration" on systems run by Anthropic and its testing partner left the models with live internet access, allowing them to breach other systems, the San Francisco-based firm said.
Anthropic said the earliest incidents date back to April and that it is "approaching the fixes as if the responsibility were ours alone."
Neither Anthropic nor the organisations that were breached had noticed the intrusions at the time.
Anthropic said it could have reviewed its records more thoroughly and added that the findings gave the firm "cautious optimism" that such risks can be overcome with more investment and tighter measures.
The incidents come as tech firms pour billions of dollars into developing AI agents that can independently perform tasks ranging from research and customer support to cybersecurity.
A string of AI-driven cyberattacks has fuelled calls for tighter safeguards and oversight of the technology, over concerns about the risks posed by increasingly powerful autonomous systems.
US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that Washington is considering measures to rein in AI tools after recent cybersecurity incidents.
Over the last week, OpenAI has taken responsibility for at least two hacking incidents involving its platforms breaching the rules of what they were directed to do.
On 21 July, the ChatGPT-maker said its agent - an AI system that can operate alone after human instruction - went rogue and escaped its test limits to hack into Hugging Face.
OpenAI said the incident was "unprecedented", and it was investigating with Hugging Face, whose boss co-founder Thomas Wolf told the BBC that the incident is "a wake-up call" for the industry.
The incidents have been viewed with some scepticism as OpenAI and Anthropic prepare for blockbuster stock market listings that are expected to value each firm at around $1tn (£740bn).
An OpenAI spokesperson has said "we recognise there are a lot of questions and speculative details circulating" about the incident. They added that "we plan to publish a technical report of our learnings in the coming weeks".

title: What your summer reading list says about you
summary: Just picked your holiday book? Our choices can subconsciously reveal important parts of our personality, studies show.
full_text:
What your summer reading list says about you
- Published
You've been dreaming about that summer break on the sun lounger, book in one hand and drink in the other, for months. Now the dash to the airport gate, train station or hours-long drive is all that stands in your way.
But what does the book you've just shoved in your suitcase say about you?
"It's definitely not a random choice," says Edgar Dubourg, a cognitive scientist at the École Normale Supérieure in Paris. "Your reading list is basically a map of your personality.
"When you pick a thriller or romance or horror or science fiction you're not escaping your psychology, in a way, you're really feeling very intuitive and very old parts of your brain.
"Fiction isn't inventing new emotions in you. It's pressing on those pre-existing motivations like instincts."
Studies have shown that our book choices can subconsciously reveal important parts of our personality - including what gives us pleasure and what makes us feel emotion.
Research by Dr Valerie van Mulukom, a senior lecturer in psychology at Oxford Brookes University, suggests that our inner anxieties (or what she calls existential insecurities) determine which book we pick from the shelf.
During her study, she used how often someone might engage with a certain genre to match it up with one of the following four clusters:
- Epic other-world adventures (action, adventure, science fiction, dystopian/post-apocalyptic, fantasy) 
- Everyday life and human relationships (comedy, romantic, drama, family, musical) 
- Threat and danger (true crime, crime/mystery/thriller, horror) 
- Facts and histories (documentary, biography, historical) 
But what do they mean? And how do they match up with our own anxieties?
Can't resist a murder mystery? You're probably intrigued by danger
If, like me, you're big on crime novels, then this suggests you're concerned with - or intrigued by - threat and danger.
This isn't just limited to old-fashioned detective novels or psychological thrillers, but can be anything from true crime and spy stories to supernatural horrors like the works of Stephen King's books.
The UK bestseller lists have a range of titles that sit in the "threat and danger" category defined by the research, including:
- The Secret of Secrets by Dan Brown (Penguin) 
- The Family Friend by Claire Douglas (Penguin) 
- London Falling by Patrick Radden Keefe (Picador) 
Beach bag full of romance novels? You likely worry about your relationships
Meanwhile, if lustful romance is more your thing (very much not mine), then your insecurities are more likely to be about your relationships, both romantic and platonic, and your thoughts on social status and reputation.
The UK bestseller lists have a range of titles that sit in the "everyday life and human relationships" category defined by the research, including:
- The Correspondent by Virginia Evans (Penguin) 
- The Names by Florence Knapp (Phoenix) 
- Heartstopper Volume 6 by Alice Oseman (Hodder) 
Spending summer in Westeros? You may be someone who worries about humanity's future
At the opposite end, someone who likes science fiction or fantasy novels tends to be more concerned with the state of the world.
If you're spending your summer holiday finally reading the Game of Thrones novels, known for mixing political intrigue and medieval battles with tales of dragons and undead armies, then you're likely to be someone who worries about climate change or the threat of war.
The UK bestseller lists have a range of titles that sit in the "epic other-world adventures" category defined by the research, including:
- Duskbound by Bree Grenwich and Parker Lennox (Penguin) 
- Red Dwarf: Titan by Rob Grant and Andrew Marshall (Gollancz) 
- To Flame a Wild Flower by Sarah A Parker (HarperVoyager) 
Prefer non-fiction? You might be searching for answers rather than adventures
For me, holiday reading is serious work. On my last trip abroad, I took eight books for a three-week holiday, ranging from Frank Herbert's sci-fi epic Dune to James Ellroy's noir throwback The Black Dahlia.
But not everyone likes disappearing off into fictional worlds. What if autobiographies or books about history are more your thing?
Dr Dubourg says it is narratives that are important, not necessarily whether they're fact or fiction.
"Everybody consumes narratives, be it in the form of actual news, of anecdotes, of stories that people tell in neighbourhoods."
The UK bestseller lists have a range of titles that sit in the "facts and history" category defined by the research, including:
- Regime Change by Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan (Simon & Schuster) 
- Mother Mary Comes to Me by Arundhati Roy (Penguin) 
- Careless People by Sarah Wynn-Williams (Pan) 
So next time you pick up a book, what you think is just something vaguely interesting might actually make up an important part of your psychology.

title: 'I pay £580 a month to live in a disused care home': Property guardians show us around
summary: Could you live communally in a disused building in exchange for a heavily discounted rent? Property guardians show us around.
full_text:
'I pay £580 a month to live in a disused care home': Property guardians show us around
- Published
Would you live in a disused care home, pub or bank in exchange for a heavily discounted rent?
As cost of living pressures persist, a growing number of people are applying to become so-called property guardians - living in vacant residential or commercial buildings to protect them from squatters, vandalism and disrepair.
They typically pay 30-50% less rent than private tenants, sometimes with bills thrown in, In exchange for looking after the buildings.
However property guardians also have significantly fewer rights than private renters and can be evicted with just 28 days' notice.
Katrina, 29, has spent the last 10 months living with around 50 other people in an Edwardian mansion in Hampstead, London, which was used as a care home until 2015.
The postgraduate student, who says she could not afford to rent privately in the capital, currently pays £580 a month for her room including bills and council tax, about £400 below the London average, external.
Katrina says guardianship gives her the chance to live in an unusual property and describes the mansion as an "incredible" and "romantic" place despite it being "quite run down".
Set in 1.7 acres of gardens, the building has grand staircases, south-west-facing balconies and chandeliers in some rooms, but it does have some downsides: "We've had mushrooms growing on the walls, leaks, parts of the balcony stonework have fallen off," says Katrina.
Katrina says she loves the communal aspect of guardianship, which is "somewhere between living in university halls, a block of flats and a fancy squat".
She lives with "all sorts of people", from lawyers to artists, sharing bathrooms, a kitchen and communal living areas, and regularly socialising.
But there are disagreements over things like noise, she says. And while Lowe, the company that manages the property, operates a stringent vetting process for its guardians, two residents have been asked to leave because of antisocial behaviour - one for alleged sexual harassment.
Lowe tells the BBC it acts "quickly and decisively" on the rare occasion someone breaches its standards and that the "overwhelming majority" of guardians go on to be "brilliant, community-minded residents".
'It's really precarious'
In general, guardians have fewer rights than private renters, external because they hold a "licence to occupy" rather than a tenancy.
Guardianship companies are not obliged to protect their deposits or carry out repairs not specifically provided for in the agreement. Landlords can also visit at any time, without warning, and evict residents without giving a reason.
Katrina admits she worries about the temporary nature of her arrangement sometimes. A developer bought the former care home last year and plans to turn it into flats, so she will eventually have to leave.
"It's really precarious in that sense. It's not guaranteed to last. If anyone doesn't like that, it's not for them," she says.
Last year, the Property Guardian Providers Association (PGPA) estimated there were between 10,000 and 15,000 property guardians in the UK, mainly in major cities, with most aged between 20 and 35.
The trade group says the number of people applying has risen sharply as rental costs soar.
David Hale, 32, became a guardian almost 10 years ago to save money and has never lived in standard rental accommodation.
He and his wife now rent a "massive" space at a former primary school in Brixton, South London, for around £1,500 a month, including bills and council tax. He says they wouldn't be able to afford a similar property otherwise and save about £1,000 a month.
Tips on becoming a property guardian
- Prepare to be flexible: You may stay for several years, or you may need to move on with relatively short notice. 
- Choose an established guardian company: Look for a reputable provider with good health and safety procedures 
- Read your licence agreement carefully: Understand your responsibilities to the building, house rules and visitor policies 
- Know your rights: Guardians are legally entitled to a court order before they can be evicted and their home must be safe to live in 
- Embrace community living: Be considerate of those you live with and respect shared areas. 
Sources: the Property Guardian Providers Association, Shelter, Ad Hoc Property Management
Around 20 guardians live in the school's open classrooms and offices, sharing a kitchen and large garden.
But while David has enjoyed communal living, he and his wife are saving to buy their own home: "We wouldn't want to share toilets and bathrooms forever. We also want to start a family."
The PGPA believes guardianship could help ease the UK's housing crisis by providing affordable temporary accommodation for thousands of people.
It points out that over a million homes currently stand empty, along with tens of millions of square feet, external of non-residential property.
But housing charity Shelter argues the rise of property guardianship shows how people are being forced "further and further afield just to keep a roof over their heads".
"For most, this isn't a good alternative to an affordable, stable home," says chief executive Sarah Elliott.

title: Teen hackers tell BBC how police are helping them use their skills for good
summary: Cyber Prevent is targeting predominantly boys and young men at risk of being drawn to cyber criminality.
full_text:
Teen hackers tell BBC how police are helping them use their skills for good
- Published
Lucas was 16 when he got into trouble for hacking his school computers. Twice.
"It was like a challenge to see if I could," he told the BBC.
He wanted access to play games and visit blocked websites so he started tinkering with programming.
At one point he even unscrewed the computer tower to take some internal components home for tests.
"It's quite a sense of achievement when you've succeeded in doing something that two or three trained professionals have spent a lot of time trying to stop you doing," he said.
He was close to being expelled - but his worried mother had no idea how serious his actions were.
She called the police and invited an officer from the nationwide programme Cyber Choices to their home in rural Cumbria.
"My mum was like, 'ooh, you've got a detective coming to speak to you, you're in a lot of trouble'," Lucas said.
"So I was sat at the window waiting. Who's going to come? How much trouble am I going to be in?"
PC Sam Cooper, a cyber prevent officer, knocked on the door earlier this year and he has been working with Lucas ever since.
He explained to Lucas, as he has with dozens of other children, there are real consequences and harm caused by cyber-attacks.
Cooper said showing the mostly teenage boys what was legal and not was step one.
Then comes positive encouragement over months of one-to-one meetings, usually at their homes.
"I'll try and find where their interests are and try and divert them towards professional training, qualifications," he said.
Cyber Choices, also known as Cyber Prevent, is like a hacker rehab course.
It works in parallel with the more well-known Prevent scheme, which identifies potential terror offenders.
While at Lucas's house I saw first hand how some of the conversations work.
Lucas enthusiastically explained his latest computer experiments and Cooper asked him what software and tools he was using to check they were legitimate.
Soon the officer will take Lucas on a visit to the local university where he will be shown the cyber security course with the aim of inspiring him to apply.
More than 1,150 cases have been referred to the National Crime Agency (NCA)'s Cyber Choices scheme in the last eight years - nearly 600 of those were in the last three years.
Authorities warn teenage hacking groups are playing an increasingly prominent role in serious cyber-attacks.
Young, English-speaking hackers have been linked to attacks on major organisations including Transport for London (TfL) and MGM Grand in 2024, and Marks and Spencer and the Co-op in 2025.
Individuals are also being increasingly targeted in hacks for their cryptocurrency holdings.
"It certainly has become more of a problem," said Paul Foster, who leads cyber prevention work at the NCA.
"Certainly English-speaking, western world individuals that we know are now more active in cyber-crime."
He said young people were engaged with online activity and devices at increasingly young ages exposing them to criminal communities and influences.
Police say many young offenders do not initially set out to become criminals.
Instead, they often begin by experimenting with technology, testing systems or trying to bypass restrictions before becoming drawn into online communities where hacking is encouraged.
'Majority are neurodiverse'
The children can come from all over the country and from a range of backgrounds, and Cooper said many have autism or are neurodiverse.
"The vast majority of individuals I'm dealing with are neurodiverse," he said.
"Even if they're not labelled as such... they obviously have more affinity with computers than they do with practical and social reality," he said.
"Sometimes they can get fixated on certain goals and not listen to any adults around them, so that's where I come in and sit them down and talk to them."
In 2023, a high profile teenage hacker called Arion Kurtaj, who had hacked Grand Theft Auto maker Rockstar Games, was deemed unfit to stand trial due to his autism.
Two teen hackers who were jailed earlier this month for the TfL hack were also autistic - which was taken into account by the judge when he sentence them to five and half years in prison.
One of them, Owen Flowers from Walsall, had been offered a chance to enrol on the Cyber Choices programme when he first got into trouble shortly after he turned 16.
He refused to engage with the scheme.
Some critics argue that teaching cyber skills to young people who have already shown an interest in hacking risks making them more capable offenders.
In another ongoing court case, it emerged a teenager who had been enrolled on the programme was alleged to have gone on to commit further offences.
Foster said he understood the concern but believes the alternative would be worse.
"My fear is that if we didn't give them something like Cyber Choices, where would they get that input and where would that input take them?"
The NCA hoped it could intervene before curiosity, talent and online influence turn into serious offending.
For Lucas, the fear of having a police officer show up at his door made him rethink things.
He admits that if he had not been caught and helped by the scheme he would have carried on pushing boundaries in his exploration of computers and hacking.
Meanwhile in Leicestershire, 21-year-old cyber-security professional Izak is another Cyber Choices success story.
At 15 he hacked his school computers so he could make graphic designs in Photoshop, but he also found himself drawn into cyber criminal groups online who were making "lots of money".
A visit from Leicestershire Police got him onto the programme and helped him see cyber-security as a possible job opportunity, by encouraging him to "use my cyber skills for good".

title: Millions opposed military rule in Myanmar. Is their dream of a revolution over?
summary: Opponents of the junta hoped a revolution would remake Myanmar - but these are disheartening times.
full_text:
Millions opposed military rule in Myanmar. Is their dream of a revolution over?
- Published
"One day we will get our freedom back."
The 22-year-old has spent much of his adult life fighting for it. But now, after five years of civil war in Myanmar, he has had enough of war and political struggle.
"I want to help our people as much as I can. But I choose another way. A non-violent way."
The young man is part of a huge exodus of people from Myanmar seeking sanctuary in the Thai border town of Mae Sot.
He spoke to the BBC from a small, dark room tucked away down a back street – one of a network of safe houses set up by charities to help new arrivals.
Most have very little. They are exhausted, traumatised by their experiences in Myanmar, and very vulnerable. With no legal status in Thailand, the safe houses are their only refuge.
He was 17 when he joined the nationwide protests against the military coup in Myanmar in 2021.
When these were crushed by the army, like many young protesters he travelled to an area controlled by ethnic insurgents to get military training.
He returned to Yangon as part of an urban guerrilla squad, planting bombs outside targets like police stations. "I thought then that non-violent protests were not the right way to get back our freedom."
But he was soon caught and sentenced to seven years in Insein prison, notorious for its brutal treatment of inmates.
He was released last year, and fled to Mae Sot because of the intense police surveillance of his family at their home in Yangon. It is for their sake that he does not want to use his name.
For the millions of Burmese who have risked their lives and left their homes to oppose military rule, these are disheartening times.
They have been dreaming of a revolution which will remake Myanmar as a more democratic and inclusive country, and purge the armed forces from politics.
Instead, they are watching the man they hold responsible for igniting the civil war strengthen his hold on power.
Last month Myanmar's military ruler General Min Aung Hlaing was given a red-carpet welcome by China's Xi Jinping, capping a joint effort by both countries to transform his image from blood-stained dictator to civilian president, increasingly accepted, if not respected, by neighbouring countries.
Chinese diplomatic and military support has been critical in helping the man who deposed the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi in 2021 to recover from the catastrophic consequences of his coup.
Over the past year the military junta recaptured much of the territory it had lost to the hundreds of insurgent groups which formed to resist the coup.
A stage-managed election earlier this year, from which the main opposition groups were excluded, has now allowed Min Aung Hlaing to present himself as a legitimate, elected leader.
So where does that leave those who had hoped for a very different future? Many are effectively trapped in Mae Sot.
The town is the main gateway for trade between Myanmar and Thailand, and has always had a large, though fluctuating Burmese population. This has been swollen by refugees since the coup. But you rarely see them outside.
Most are undocumented. They got here unofficially, by crossing the narrow Moei river which marks the border, and live in constant fear of arrest and deportation by the Thai police.
They also fear reprisals against family members back in Myanmar. One former army officer, who defected to the opposition three years ago, told the BBC she only dares leave the room she rents in Mae Sot twice a month.
For those who have just arrived, the safe houses offer them short-term shelter, usually for a maximum of six months. These are warrens of small rooms with basic communal facilities, hidden down the city's smaller side-streets.
Behind every door is a harrowing personal story.
The young urban guerilla who was imprisoned in Insein jail described routine torture and sexual assault by the guards. He also says prison was where he had a change of heart about the struggle.
"I had hoped the revolution would be better. But they did not unite at all [the insurgent groups], they fought each other and I did not like that situation. I saw many casualties from the war, and I could not bear to see things like that."
As the eldest child, he also felt he couldn't risk his life and abandon his family. "So I gave up the armed struggle – not only the armed struggle but other kinds of struggle too, like in politics. I want to help our people in another way."
He has dedicated himself to teaching children in the safe house, and to supporting as best he can friends who are still in prison.
"I try to give them hope that the revolution is not finished yet, and that we still have a chance to win."
Our presence in the safe house drew a crowd of other residents, all with different stories to tell.
There were former members of the people's defence forces which have been fighting against the junta. There was an official from Aung San Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy, and several young men avoiding forced conscription into the army.
A common refrain among them was that, while they all still believed in the revolution, after five years they were exhausted and needed to earn money for their families. Mae Sot was their only option.
Also here was Yin Yin Aung, a 20-year-old woman with her husband and young son.
They had made an epic, 1,000-mile journey to reach Mae Sot from Sagaing, a region which has put up some of the strongest resistance to the military coup, and suffered terrible reprisals, including relentless air strikes.
Her village, Htomar, was sandwiched between a military base and an insurgent-controlled area. She described the day more than two years ago when soldiers occupied the village, firing their weapons and driving the population ahead of them.
"When the phone signal was cut, we knew something was going to happen. I heard three gunshots, and saw people running between the houses shouting that an army column was coming. We could not carry much. My father took a bag of rice so we would have something to eat, and we ran until we reached a place deep in the forest and hills."
There was nothing there, she adds, so they had to drink the river water, which they also used for bathing, and as a toilet. They fell sick and some of them died. But they stayed in the forest for six months.
The soldiers left the village after one month, but Yin Yin says it had been thoroughly looted, with landmines laid around the houses.
No-one dared move back.
During this time she gave birth to her son, but he has an abdominal hernia which needs surgery.
Over several weeks the family made their way south and east, arriving six months ago in Mae Sot. This is the second safe house they have lived in; they had reached the maximum stay allowed in the first.
They are trying to avoid having to rent a room commercially so she can save up for her son's operation.
Not everyone is disheartened by the military's successes.
In another safe house we met a former Yangon bartender-turned-rebel, with his wife and two month-old-baby.
They had left war-torn Karen State, where he is a member of the Cobra Column, one of the more effective fighting units in the opposition, and come to Mae Sot to have their baby.
But he seemed eager to get back to the war.
"I believe that the revolution we are fighting right now will succeed one day. Because they [the military] are fighting a war against the entire country. They are fighting a war against the very citizens they are supposed to protect and safeguard. There is no way they can win."
The Cobra Column fights alongside the Karen National Union, which is relatively well-armed and has been fighting the central government for nearly 80 years. Morale is still high there.
But other people's defence forces are struggling this year, after Chinese pressure cut their supplies of weapons and technology. Meanwhile the Myanmar military has benefitted from training and new equipment from Russia and Ch
